items.explanation_en: Each name should be matched by era and role: philosopher-educator of the Spring and Autumn Period, Western Han diplomat, Ming diplomat, and Ming physician.
items.draft_answer: Match each picture by era and profession: Confucius goes with the Spring and Autumn philosopher and educator, Zhang Qian with the Western Han diplomat and explorer, Zheng He with the Ming diplomat and explorer, and Li Shizhen with the Ming physician and medical scholar. The clues in each caption are the dynasty and the occupation, so reading them first makes the pairing straightforward.

items.explanation_en: A personal response is expected; support your choice with one or two concrete deeds of the person you admire.
items.draft_answer: I admire Zheng He most, because he turned a childhood curiosity about distant places into seven voyages that reached Arabia and East Africa. He had been trained at court and appointed to command a fleet of more than 200 junks, yet what strikes me is his patience in negotiating trade pacts instead of simply showing force. From him I learn that curiosity, preparation and respect for other peoples can make one person a bridge between cultures.

items.explanation_en: Para. 1: the elderly men told the journalist they were descendants of Chinese sailors whose boat was shipwrecked on Pate centuries earlier.
Para. 2 compares 27,000 crew with Columbus' 1,500 and much larger junks, implying Zheng He's fleet far outclassed Columbus'.
The quotation marks signal reservation: the Indian Ocean was already known and visited by other peoples, so 'discovered' is not literally true.
Para. 4: from a young age he read books by great scholars such as Confucius and Mencius.
Para. 6: in 1405 the emperor appointed him with a royal order to establish ties with rulers all around the Indian Ocean.
Para. 7: rulers were impressed by his diplomatic skills and the elaborate gifts he brought, and agreed to send ambassadors to the Ming court.
Para. 9: the war in the north drew military investment away from fleet maintenance, and the court turned to building and expanding the Great Wall.
Para. 10: the voyages pushed the limits of ships' size, complexity and range, and helped spread gunpowder and the compass.
Support your view with the text's evidence: trade pacts, ambassadors, and the spread of gunpowder and the compass.
items.draft_answer: Zheng He's voyages opened sea routes linking China with Southeast Asia, Arabia and East Africa, and they built ties through trade pacts and exchanged envoys rather than through conquest. Because his fleet brought silk, porcelain and elaborate gifts and returned with ambassadors, later travelers inherited a model of communication based on mutual respect. The expeditions also carried Chinese technologies such as the compass and gunpowder outward, changing how distant societies navigated and traded.

items.explanation_en: Anchor your answer in concrete steps such as language study, cultural knowledge and real exchange experience.
items.draft_answer: I can begin by knowing my own culture well enough to explain it, reading classics such as Confucius and Mencius just as Zheng He did. Learning foreign languages and histories would let me speak to others in terms they understand, and joining exchange or volunteer programs would give me real practice. Above all, I should stay curious about other cultures and respectful of differences, as Zheng He was with the rulers he met.

items.explanation_en: Relate the meaning of life to the text's themes of curiosity, service and lasting contribution.
items.draft_answer: Zheng He's story suggests that a life gains meaning through curiosity and service rather than through possessions. He spent nearly thirty years at sea and used his voyages to build friendships between peoples, not merely to collect treasures. For me this means choosing work that connects people and leaving behind something that outlasts my own career.

items.explanation_en: Dense collocates with forests to mean thickly grown, matching 'tropical rain forests and giant waterfalls'.
'Be appointed to do sth.' takes the past participle: a new manager was appointed to take charge of the project.
The blank is the third item in the gerund series 'cooking, cleaning, and ...', so 'escorting' (escort sb to a place).
'Is patrolling the roads' uses the present continuous for an ongoing action; patrol takes a direct object.
'Despite its complexity' needs a noun after the possessive; complexity means the state of being complicated.
'Economic expansion' is the fixed collocation for growth in the size of an economy.
'A vague plan of action' means an unclear, imprecise plan; vague is the adjective modifying plan.
'Maintenance period' is the routine servicing period a ship completes before setting out on a new mission.
'In both the digital and physical realms' - the 'both ... and' structure requires the plural realms.
'Frail elderly people' means weak, physically delicate old people; frail modifies people, parallel to 'two children'.
'Normalize the relations between the two countries' means bring relations back to normal, ending years of hostility.
'Familiarize ourselves with new devices' is the reflexive collocation meaning to get to know something.
'A(n) dictator' needs a noun after the article; a dictator refuses to listen to other people's advice.
The passive 'should not be privatized' requires the past participle of privatize.
'A(n) investigator' is the person noun from investigate, the one sent to look into the cause of the fire.
'Ability to standardize its services' takes the base verb after to; standardize means make uniform in quality.
'Have been widely publicized' is present perfect passive, so the past participle of publicize is required.
'Now we will summarize what we have learned' - modal will takes the base form; summarize means give a brief account.
'Promote trade and diplomacy with other states' - diplomacy is the parallel noun to trade in interstate relations.
'Talented in many realms' - plural realms after 'many', meaning fields or areas of ability.
'Appointed Zheng He as the commander' - appoint sb as sth, in the past tense for the year 1403.
'Epic exploration journeys' - epic as an adjective meaning grand and heroic in scale.
The list 'spices, ivory, ... animals, and other goods' needs an adjective; exotic means foreign and unusual.
'Made trade pacts with the rulers' - pacts collocates with trade and with made, meaning formal agreements.
'Brought back ambassadors of various states' - the envoys sent to meet the Ming emperor.
'Promoted the expansion of China's cultural and economic influence' - expansion is the noun from expand.
'Forged new, friendly ties' - past tense, and forge ties is the fixed collocation for building relationships.
'The history of ocean navigation' - navigation names the skill of planning and directing a ship's course.
'Be in charge of their own learning' means take responsibility for directing it themselves.
The passive 'is viewed as an occasion' uses view ... as, with the past participle after is.
'Nations that have traded with China for years' - the present perfect needs the past participle traded.
'Special events take place every day' - the plural subject takes the base form; take place means happen.
'Was fully loaded with 50 containers of goods' - be loaded with means be filled with cargo.
'Last month, the polar icebreaker set off from the port' - past tense of set off, meaning start a journey.
'Have long been curious about what goes on inside the space station' - be curious about means eager to know.
'You can stay here along with your friend' - along with means together with.
Paras. 4-8 open each stage with a time signal; list them in reading order and the events already fall into chronological order.
items.draft_answer: The signals are 'As a child', 'Later when he served in the royal court', 'In 1403', 'In 1405', 'During the next six expeditions', 'In 1431' and 'Toward the end of this voyage in 1433'. Arranged in order: Zheng He was born in Yunnan around 1371 and was curious about the world; he read books by Confucius and Mencius, then received military training at court; in 1403 the emperor ordered the Treasure Fleet; in 1405 he was appointed to command it; over the next six expeditions he made trade pacts and brought back ambassadors; in 1431 he sailed on the seventh voyage; and in 1433 he died of disease.

items.explanation_en: Follow the outline: introduction with a thesis, four body points in time order, and a closing statement on significance.
items.draft_answer: Zheng He, born around 1371 in Yunnan, is the Chinese explorer I admire most. As a child he questioned his father and grandfather about their travels and read Confucius and Mencius, and after military training at court he was appointed in 1405 to command a fleet of more than 200 junks. His seven voyages reached Ceylon, Arabia and East Africa, opening trade pacts and diplomatic ties and spreading gunpowder and the compass. His story shows that China's spirit of exploration helped build the modern world, and it still stands among the great wonders of ocean navigation.

items.explanation_en: Fact: a specific, checkable event in Para. 3 - Audrey was seized and put in line for a work camp.
Fact: a verifiable move recorded in Para. 5, after the war ended.
Opinion: 'beautifully' is director Billy Wilder's aesthetic judgment, not something that can be verified.
Opinion: an evaluative claim about her character in Para. 7, which cannot be measured or checked.
Opinion: reported praise from friends - an assessment of personality rather than an observable fact.
Fact: a dated appointment in 1988 that can be documented, from Para. 9.
Fact: a specific family event recorded in Para. 12, with named people and an occasion.
Opinion: value-laden words such as 'gracious', 'charm' and 'kindness' express praise, not verifiable fact.
Paras. 2 and 6: she felt her most significant work was humanitarian work for UNICEF, not her film roles.
Para. 3 says 'her family was bankrupted as a result of the invasion'; the other options contradict the text.
Para. 4: she refused to let her spirit be afflicted and 'transcended those challenges' instead of giving in.
Para. 5: after arriving in the U.K. she was spotted by a producer and landed a role in Roman Holiday.
Para. 8: the Swiss home was 'a paradise where she could hide from the world with her beloved family'.
Para. 10: she made missions into bleak, war-torn destinations such as Somalia, Sudan and Vietnam.
Para. 11: 'she believed deeply in the ideology that all people share in the duty to care for those in need'.
Her generosity, compassion and UNICEF service run through the whole text, so 'kind-hearted' fits best.
Draw on Audrey Hepburn's career in the text: rigorous training, being spotted, and purpose beyond fame.
items.draft_answer: I think talent matters, but a willingness to work relentlessly matters more. Audrey Hepburn kept a rigorous schedule at a famous ballet school before a producer spotted her, and she went on improving her craft long after she became famous. Beyond skill, a sense of purpose beyond fame gave her career its durability, which is why she valued her humanitarian work above her film roles.

items.explanation_en: Use the text's explanation of Audrey's motive: remembered suffering plus the influence success brings.
items.draft_answer: People who have suffered themselves often remember how it felt, and that memory turns into sympathy for others. Audrey Hepburn was malnourished and nearly sent to a work camp, so she understood what the children she later visited needed. Success also gives people money, fame and influence that can be turned into help, as she did by accepting one dollar a year as a UNICEF ambassador.

items.explanation_en: Name one figure and give a concrete deed or idea, then link it to the charity theme of Text B.
items.draft_answer: I would name Mencius, who taught that one should extend the care given to one's own elders and children to the elders and children of others. That idea is the root of charity in Chinese thought: kindness is not a favor to strangers but a duty we all share. It matches Audrey Hepburn's belief that all people share in the duty to care for those in need.

items.explanation_en: 'Physically dangerous situations' - the adverb modifies the adjective dangerous, parallel to 'emotionally draining'.
'His writing, which retains an echo of his love of nature' - third-person singular verb agrees with writing.
'The vast realm of nature' - vast means immense in extent, fitting 'realm'.
'The movement and mixing of populations spread different cultures' - past tense; spread is invariable in form.
'Elaborate gifts or local specialties' - elaborate means carefully made with much detail.
'Surprising encounters with places with a mysterious past' - present participle used as an adjective.
'He lived in overwhelming misery' - overwhelming intensifies the noun misery, meaning crushing hardship.
'The desperate reality of poverty' - desperate means hopeless and extremely serious.
'No hardship could jeopardize his hope' - the modal could takes the base form jeopardize.
'The long voyage of life' - long is the adjective describing the duration of the voyage.
'Emotionally draining periods' - the adverb modifies the participle draining, parallel to 'physically dangerous'.
'Success which perpetually signifies your devotion' - the adverb of frequency sits before the verb it modifies.
Key renderings: 不可缺少的 as 'indispensable', 众口难调 as 'hard to please everyone', 与时俱进 as 'keeping pace with the times'.
